title: DIY Bedroom Drawer Organizer Tutorial: Complete Step-by-Step Guide 2026
excerpt: Learn how to make your own bedroom drawer organizer with easy-to-find materials. Complete step-by-step tutorial for an organized bedroom in 2026.

• **Save budget** compared to buying ready-made organizers priced Rp 192.000 - Rp 480.000

Research from [Houzz.com](https://www.houzz.com) shows that homes with good organizational systems can increase residents' productivity by up to 40%. Starting from the bedroom is a smart step to create a [more organized home](https://www.sesoris.com).
## Materials and Tools Needed
![Materials for DIY drawer organizer such as cardboard, ruler, scissors and fabric](/images/blog/tutorial-membuat-organizer-laci-kamar-tidur-diy-materials.webp)

Before starting this drawer organizer tutorial, prepare all the following materials and tools. The total cost of making it is only around Rp 24.000 - Rp 48.000, much more economical than buying ready-made organizers.
### Main Materials:
• **Used cardboard** medium size (3-4 pieces) - free from online stores or supermarkets
• **Fabric scraps or wrapping paper** 2-3 meters for lining - Rp 16.000 - Rp 32.000
• **Double-sided tape** 1 roll size 1 inch - Rp 5.000
• **White glue** or hot glue gun - Rp 3.000 - Rp 8.000
### Equipment:
• **Ruler** at least 30 cm long
• **Sharp scissors** or cutter
• **Pencil** for marking
• **Permanent marker** (optional for labeling)

Tip from [Pinterest.com](https://www.pinterest.com): Choose fabric with patterns that match your bedroom design so the organizer is not only functional but also aesthetic. Polka dots, stripes, or geometric patterns are timeless choices.

## Step 1: Measuring and Planning Drawer Dimensions
![Process of measuring bedroom drawer dimensions with a ruler to make a DIY organizer](/images/blog/tutorial-membuat-organizer-laci-kamar-tidur-diy-measuring.webp)
The first crucial step in making a drawer organizer is accurate measurement. Any mistakes at this stage will affect the entire final result.
### How to Measure Your Drawer Correctly:
1. **Empty the drawer** completely and clean it from dust
2. **Measure the drawer's length** with a ruler (for example: 45 cm)
3. **Measure the drawer's width** (for example: 32 cm)
4. **Measure the drawer's height** minus 1 cm for movement space (for example: 8 cm)
5. **Write down all dimensions** on paper with a simple sketch
### Planning Compartments:
Based on your drawer's function, plan an optimal space division:
• **Underwear drawer**: 6-8 small compartments for bras and panties
• **Sock drawer**: 4-6 medium compartments for various sock types
• **Accessories drawer**: Combination of small and medium compartments for watches, jewelry, wallets

Pro tip: Sketch the division on paper first. This will help you visualize the final result and calculate how much cardboard you need. For [more optimal clothing storage](https://www.sesoris.com/collections), consider the division pattern that professional organizers commonly use.
## Step 2: Cutting Cardboard to Size
![Cutting cardboard to size to make bedroom drawer organizer dividers](/images/blog/tutorial-membuat-organizer-laci-kamar-tidur-diy-cutting.webp)
After careful planning, it's time to cut the cardboard into organizer components. Precision at this stage will determine how well the organizer fits inside your drawer.
### Calculating Cardboard Pieces Needed:
For a drawer measuring 45cm x 32cm x 8cm with 6 compartments:
• **2 long strips**: 45cm x 8cm (main lengthwise dividers)
• **4 short strips**: 15cm x 8cm (cross dividers)
• **1 base piece**: 44cm x 31cm x 0.5cm (optional for reinforcement)
### Proper Cutting Technique:
1. **Use a ruler** as a guide for straight lines
2. **Press the cardboard** with the ruler while cutting for neat results
3. **Cut with continuous motion** to avoid jagged lines
4. **Create slots in the middle** of strips for an interlocking system
5. **Test fit** each piece before moving to the next stage
### Creating an Interlocking Slot System:
For strong joints without additional glue:
• **Slots in long strips**: Cut a slot as wide as cardboard thickness in the middle of the strip, 4 cm deep from the top
• **Slots in short strips**: Cut a slot as wide as cardboard thickness in the middle of the strip, 4 cm deep from the bottom
• **Test the joint**: Make sure both strips can interlock tightly
According to the crafter community [Ideaonline.co.id](https://ideaonline.co.id), the interlocking technique provides 3x better structural strength than relying on glue alone.
## Step 3: Assembling the Organizer Structure
![Process of assembling cardboard dividers into a drawer organizer with various compartments](/images/blog/tutorial-membuat-organizer-laci-kamar-tidur-diy-assembling.webp)
The assembly stage is the moment that determines the strength and stability of your DIY drawer organizer. With the right technique, a homemade organizer can last 2-3 years of normal use.
### Correct Assembly Order:
1. **Start with long strips** as the main framework
2. **Install the first short strip** in the slots you've created
3. **Ensure 90-degree angles** using a ruler as a guide
4. **Continue installing** the remaining short strips with equal spacing
5. **Press all joints** firmly until they're secure and won't come loose easily
### Reinforcing Joints:
For extra durability, apply the following reinforcement techniques:
• **Apply white glue** at each slot joint
• **Hold for 2-3 minutes** until the glue starts drying
• **Add small strips** at the bottom of joints for additional support
• **Let it sit for 24 hours** before moving to the finishing stage
### Common Problem Troubleshooting:
**Joint is too loose:** Add small tape pieces on the slot sides to tighten the gap
**Joint is too tight:** Sand the slot edges lightly with fine-grit sandpaper
**Structure is unstable:** Make sure all joints are exactly 90 degrees and add glue at critical points

## Step 4: Lining with Decorative Fabric or Paper
![Lining organizer cardboard with beautiful patterned fabric using double-sided tape](/images/blog/tutorial-membuat-organizer-laci-kamar-tidur-diy-covering.webp)
This finishing stage not only makes the organizer look beautiful but also protects the cardboard from moisture and extends its lifespan. A well-lined organizer can last 3x longer than a plain one.
### Preparing Lining Materials:
• **Measure fabric needed** using the formula: (length + height x 2) + 5cm margin
• **Cut fabric** according to the size of each organizer component
• **Prepare double-sided tape** in small pieces for easier application
• **Clean the cardboard surface** from dust and loose fibers
### Neat Lining Technique:
1. **Start with the longest side** to minimize visible seams
2. **Apply double-sided tape** along the cardboard edges with 2-3 cm spacing
3. **Pull the fabric** with enough tension so it doesn't sag or wrinkle
4. **Fold corners** using the hospital corner technique for professional results
5. **Press firmly** using a ruler to ensure no air bubbles
### Hospital Corner Technique for Neat Corners:
• **Pull the fabric** to cover the cardboard corner
• **Fold diagonally** to form a triangle at the tip
• **Press inward** and tape with double-sided tape
• **Fold the remaining sides** neatly
Data from [Tokopedia.com](https://www.tokopedia.com) shows that DIY organizers with good finishing have aesthetic value equivalent to commercial products priced Rp 288.000 - Rp 576.000.
## Step 5: Finishing Touches and Details
The final touches will make your DIY drawer organizer look professionally made. These small details are what differentiate amateur results from expert-level work.
### Adding Compartment Labels:
• **Use a label printer** or write by hand with a fine marker
• **Clear categories**: "Bras", "Panties", "Formal Socks", "Casual Socks"
• **Position labels** in the top right corner of each compartment
• **Laminate labels** with clear tape for durability
### Adding a Base Padding:
For extra protection and a premium look:
• **Use fleece or thin foam** as a base
• **Cut to fit** each compartment size
• **Attach with glue** or double-sided tape at the bottom
• **Choose a contrasting color** with the lining fabric for visual appeal
### Final Quality Check:
1. **Test stability** by lifting the organizer filled with clothes
2. **Check all joints** and reinforce if needed
3. **Ensure no sharp edges** that could damage clothes
4. **Final cleaning** with a damp cloth to remove glue residue
Pro tip from [professional organizers](https://www.sesoris.com/collections): Add scented sachets in compartment corners for long-lasting fresh aroma.
## Step 6: Installing the Organizer in Your Drawer
![Final result of a neat bedroom drawer with a DIY organizer filled with neatly arranged underwear](/images/blog/tutorial-membuat-organizer-laci-kamar-tidur-diy-final-result.webp)
The final installation stage requires careful attention so the organizer fits perfectly and functions optimally. A properly installed organizer will last for years without needing adjustments.
### Installation Steps:
1. **Clean the drawer** once more from dust and debris
2. **Test fit the organizer** without forcing it in
3. **Adjust position** so there's 2-3mm clearance on each side
4. **Press gently** until the organizer sits flat on the drawer bottom
5. **Open and close the drawer** several times to ensure there's no obstruction
### Organizing the Contents:
• **Bra category**: Fold cup facing up, arrange by color
• **Panties category**: Fold into small squares, group by type
• **Socks category**: Use the Marie Kondo folding technique for space efficiency
• **Accessories category**: Group by function and frequency of use
### Maintenance Tips:
To keep your DIY organizer in good condition and always neat:
• **Vacuum the drawer** every 2 weeks to prevent dust buildup
• **Reorganize monthly** to maintain your system
• **Replace scent sachets** every 3 months
• **Check organizer condition** every 6 months and repair if damaged

After working on hundreds of DIY organizer projects, here's wisdom from expert crafters that will elevate your results to a professional level.
### Upgraded Material Selection:
• **Use double-wall corrugated cardboard** for extra strength
• **Choose canvas or denim fabric** for superior durability
• **Invest in quality glue** like E6000 for permanent joints
• **Use velcro strips** on the bottom to prevent organizer shifting
### Advanced Techniques:
• **Reinforcement corners** with small cardboard triangle brackets
• **Waterproofing** with spray coating for humid areas
• **Modular design** allowing reconfiguration anytime
• **Hidden compartments** for storing valuable items
### Advanced Troubleshooting:
**Organizer feels fragile:** Add cross-bracing underneath for structural support
**Fabric starting to peel:** Use fabric adhesive spray before applying double-sided tape
**Organizer too tall:** Trim 1-2 cm from the top of all dividers
**Compartments too small:** Redesign by removing some dividers

## FAQ: Questions About DIY Drawer Organizer
Here are answers to the most frequently asked questions about this drawer organizer tutorial:
**Q: How long-lasting is a cardboard organizer?**
With proper materials and techniques, a DIY cardboard organizer can last 2-5 years. The key is using corrugated cardboard and waterproof finishing.
**Q: What if my drawer size is non-standard?**
The beauty of DIY is total flexibility. You can adjust all dimensions to match your drawer size, even for unusual shapes.
**Q: Can I use materials other than cardboard?**
Absolutely! Thin plywood, corrugated plastic, or even bamboo can work. The construction principles remain the same, only materials and tools differ.
**Q: How do I clean the organizer if it gets dirty?**
Use a vacuum cleaner with brush attachment for dust, and a damp cloth for light stains. Avoid excessive water that could damage the cardboard.
**Q: Do I need special skills to make this?**
Not at all! This tutorial is designed for beginners. All you need is patience and care in measuring and cutting.
**Q: How long does this organizer last?**
With normal use and regular maintenance, a quality DIY organizer can last 2-5 years. Some users report using theirs for up to 7 years.
